I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt good about something I did, or maybe more confident than usual if work was going well or I handled a situation better than I expected. Nobody’s sat me down and said, “You’re wrong about reality,” or anything like that.\n\nSometimes people don’t follow what I’m saying, and then I start wondering whether I explained it badly or whether they misunderstood the order of things, but that feels different from believing something strange. I don’t think I have some fixed idea everyone is arguing with me about. At least, not that I can point to.\n\nSo… no, I don’t think so. I mean, my sleep isn’t something I’ve been tracking hour by hour, so I don’t want to sound too certain, but I haven’t noticed that I’m getting by on just a little sleep and still feeling fine or anything like that.\n\nSome nights I might not sleep great, but that’s different from not needing it, I think. If I’m short on sleep, I usually feel it. I don’t wake up feeling like, “Oh, I only got a few hours and I’m ready to go.” So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve been needing much less sleep than usual.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?\n\nPatient: Hearing voices when no one else is around… I don’t know. That’s not really how I think it started.\n\nIt’s more that I came in because when I’m trying to explain something ordinary at work, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it starts coming out wrong.
